steps.title: Class in "Jekyll and Hyde"
steps.body: Jekyll is respectable middle-class professional; Hyde represents the underclass he secretly joins. Class boundaries are both rigid and permeable.

steps.title: Effect on Structure
steps.body: Dickens's novels have cliffhangers at chapter ends because they were originally published in parts. Each installment needed to keep readers hooked.

steps.title: AO3 Context Strategy
steps.body: For the 19th century novel question, AO3 is worth 25% of marks (typically 8 out of 30 marks). Spend roughly 5-7 minutes of a 45-minute response on embedding context. Never bolt context on at the end — weave it into your argument. Examiners reward contextual points that illuminate the text, not historical facts listed for their own sake. A Grade 9 response treats context as the lens through which the text's meaning becomes clear, not a separate paragraph tagged on as an afterthought.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: How did the Industrial Revolution affect Victorian literature? | What was the Victorian "crisis of faith"? | Why were Victorians fascinated by Gothic horror?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Industrial Revolution created urban poverty, class division, and working conditions that novelists critiqued. Dickens exposed poverty; Shelley questioned science; Stevenson explored repression. | Darwin's evolution theory challenged Biblical creation. Geology showed earth was older than Bible suggested. Science undermined religious certainty, creating doubt and debate. | Despite scientific progress, Victorians feared what progress might unleash. Gothic expressed anxieties about science, degeneration, and the dark side of respectability. Hyde represents primitive urges
